items.title: Dave Bailey and John McNeil Interview, 1959-10-25
items.q: I played with them. I played with them. ... See because before it was named after Jackson, it was the Jackson band.

ctx.x: Oh yeah, well I know Ernest Paulin. He lived right back here.

Back on Seventh Street out of the cemetery between Franklin and Liberty. Ernest Paulin is his name. They called him Doc. I was playing his band. And when he got through the Gondis, they weren't Jimmy Jackson's band no more. He was four, he signed a job for ten men and he brought nine. Well he got that money, man.

items.title: Crescent City Crystals: Dave Bailey, Harold Christophe, Albert Delone, Sylvester Handy Interview, 1963-11-13
items.q: Who was the leader of that band? St. John, uh... We had a fellow by the name of Jimmy Jackson.

ctx.x: I worked with Stutter. What brass bands, what brass bands you worked with?
I worked with, uh, that's the only two brass bands I worked with. No, three. Yeah. A fellow named Jimmy Jackson, he died. Uh-huh.
What instrument did he play? Well, he used to play snare drum.
